accused_victim_relationship: Prior enmity/dispute: the accused and the informant's party were in inimical terms over non-voting in elections; this was noted by the trial judge and the Supreme Court said it could not justify disregarding the eye witnesses
statutory_provisions: IPC s.302 r/w s.149 (conviction); charged with IPC ss.302, 323, 324 r/w s.149 and s.148; Explosive Substances Act ss.3 and 4 against the appellant
weapon: Lathis, farsa (axe-like weapon) and handmade bombs (explosive); the deceased was killed by a handmade bomb thrown on his chest
evidence_type: Eyewitness (related injured witnesses), medical (autopsy and injury reports, MLC), recovery (seized weapons and bloodstained soil), FIR
aggravating_circumstances: Accused came armed with lethal weapons as aggressors; bomb thrown at the deceased's chest with pre-determined mind; several witnesses injured
trial_court_outcome: Acquitted all six accused, disbelieving the prosecution story (noting free fight, discrepancies, interested witnesses, no independent evidence)
high_court_outcome: State's appeal (Crl. A. No. 214 of 1995) allowed; acquittal reversed; appellant convicted under s.302 r/w s.149 IPC and sentenced to rigorous imprisonment for life, with other sentences concurrent
neutral_facts: On a morning in January 1984, a group of men including the accused came to the house of the victim's family armed with lathis, a farsa and handmade bombs. They began abusing the family and threatened that they would not leave the family alive. One of the accused allegedly hurled a handmade bomb at a family member, causing leg injuries, and another accused threw a handmade bomb onto the chest of the victim, who suffered serious burn and laceration injuries. Other accused used lathis, and a farsa was used to injure a woman on her hand. The victim, who was declared brought dead at hospital, was the subject of a post-mortem examination, which recorded extensive burns and lacerated wounds on the chest and hand and found the death homicidal, caused by an explosive substance. Several family members who were present were also injured and were examined by a doctor, and their injuries were proved by medical reports. The complainant lodged a First Information Report shortly after the incident. The investigating officer prepared a spot map, collected bloodstained soil, and seized the lathis, the farsa and the handmade bombs at the instance of the accused. Several other persons who were present were not examined as witnesses. The accused gave a version that the complainant's side had confined a man who later died.
physical_harm: Death of the deceased from a bomb blast injury to the chest (extensive haemorrhage, shock, lung compression); the eye witnesses also suffered blast, incised and abrasion injuries
number_of_offences: 6 charged (IPC ss.302, 323, 324, 148 read with s.149; Explosive Substances Act ss.3 and 4 against the appellant); 1 finally upheld (IPC s.302 r/w s.149)
premeditation_planning: Found: the Supreme Court accepted that the bomb was thrown with a pre-determined mind after the accused came armed to the house
motive: Immediate trigger accepted by the court: objection to abuses hurled by the accused. Alleged earlier enmity over non-voting was noted but not treated as a ground to discard eye witnesses
key_evidence_accepted: Testimony of four injured eye witnesses (PW-7, PW-14, PW-15, PW-16); autopsy evidence of PW-13; injury reports and MLC reports; FIR contents; consistent with medical evidence
witness_credibility: Court found injured related eye witnesses reliable, consistent with each other on material particulars, supported by medical evidence and FIR; minor contradictions treated as natural and insignificant
trial_duration: offence: 7.1.1984; trial judgment: not given; High Court: 12.12.2005; Supreme Court: 08.04.2015
legal_representation: Accused/appellant: Varinder Kumar Sharma, Vipin Kumar, K. K. Shrivastava (for Deepak Goel). State: C. D. Singh
investigation_status: FIR lodged (Ex. P-24); spot map, seizure of weapons, chemical examination; charge sheet filed and case committed to Sessions; trial completed
appeal_history: Trial court: acquitted all accused. High Court: State appeal allowed, convicted under s.302 r/w s.149 with life imprisonment. Supreme Court: appellant's appeal dismissed
prosecution_argument: Findings of acquittal were perverse; discrepancies were minor; injured related witnesses were reliable; non-examination of other witnesses not fatal; appellant liable under s.149 without individual overt act
defence_argument: Appellate interference with acquittal only for perversity; trial judge's view was plausible; interested witnesses; failure to examine other eye witnesses unexplained; appellant caused no injury so s.302 conviction unwarranted
legal_principle_applied: Scope of appellate interference with acquittal (plausible view test, perversity, compelling reasons); evidence of injured and related witnesses assessed as reliable; mere presence with common object of unlawful assembly attracts s.149 liability without individual overt act
precedent_relied_upon: Gamini Bala Koteswara Rao v. State of A.P (2009) 10 SCC 636; Kallu v. State of M.P (2006) 10 SCC 313; Ramesh Babulal Doshi v. State of Gujarat (1996) 9 SCC 225; Ganpat v. State of Haryana (2010) 12 SCC 59; State of Punjab v. Karnail Singh (2003) 11 SCC 271; Jugendra Singh v. State of UP (2012) 6 SCC 297; Basappa v. State of Karnataka (2014) 5 SCC 154; Dalip Singh v. State of Punjab AIR 1953 SC 364; Hari Obula Reddy v. State of A.P (1981) 3 SCC 675; Masalti v. State of UP AIR 1965 SC 202; Bhargavan v. State of Kerala (2004) 12 SCC 414; Ramachandran v. State of Kerala (2011) 9 SCC 257; State of A.P v. Gian Chand (2001) 6 SCC 71; Takhaji Hiraji v. Thakore Kubersing Chamansingh (2001) 6 SCC 145; Dahari v. State of UP (2012) 10 SCC 256; Abdul Sayeed v. State of M.P (2010) 10 SCC 259; State of Punjab v. Jagir Singh (1974) 3 SCC 277
judicial_aggravating_factors: Accused were aggressors who came armed with lethal weapons, hurled abuses, and a bomb was thrown at the deceased with pre-determined mind
